HECAP topics

Research topics of the INSPIRE-HEP literature, defined from scratch by clustering its own citation network, with no outside taxonomy: two papers share a topic when they cite each other densely. — papers in — topics and — areas, from the tables of restrepo/inspireauth10 (INSPIRE-HEP downloaded on 2026-11-09), all papers including those with more than 10 authors. The Method tab says how.

Papers per year by area

Only papers with a topic. INSPIRE's coverage changes with time: it took in most of astro-ph around 2003–2007 and much of quant-ph lately, which shows in the astrophysics and quantum physics areas.

Growing, stable and shrinking topics

A topic's trend compares its share of all papers with a topic in 2021–2025 with its share in 2011–2015, so the growth of the whole literature (×1.32 between the two periods) is taken out: Growing when the share rose by more than half (×1.5), Shrinking when it fell by more than a third (below ×0.67), Stable otherwise. The trend is also in the Topics table and in the data (topics.jsonl.gz). The details of every shrinking topic (Topics tab) show its citation network over the years.

Where the authors of a topic went

Each author with an INSPIRE profile gets a main topic in a period: the topic with most of their papers, each paper counting 1/number of authors, papers with more than 10 authors left out. Authors with at least 2 papers in the early period are followed to the late period: their main topic there, or stopped when they have no paper with a topic in it (left the field, retired, or now publish only in large collaborations). Profiles cover most but not all authors.

On the map of the topics

Arrows from the selected topic to the topics its authors moved to, width by authors; or the largest moves between any two topics. Click a topic to select it.

Where the most cited papers are cited from

The 300 most cited papers of the network, each bar split by the area of the papers that cite it. One color means a paper used inside its own field; many colors, a paper every area uses. Reach is the exponential of the Shannon entropy of the shares: 1 when all citations come from one area, 6 when the six areas cite it equally. Only citations between papers with a topic are counted.

Disruptive and consolidating papers

The CD index (Funk & Owen-Smith 2017; Park, Leahey & Funk 2023) looks at the later papers that cite a paper or its references: ni cite the paper only, nj the paper and some of its references, nk only its references; D = (ni − nj) / (ni + nj + nk). Near +1 the paper replaced what came before (disruptive); near −1 it is read together with its sources (consolidating). CD5 counts the first five years; All years has no limit, for papers recognized late. Papers up to 2020 with at least 5 references in the network.

Share of disruptive papers by year

Areas of a country

Share of the country's papers in each area, against the share of all papers with a topic. A paper counts for every country of its authors' affiliations.

Topics of the country

Specialization: the topic's share of the country's papers divided by its share of all papers with a topic; above 1, the country publishes relatively more in it. Topics with 30 or more of the country's papers. Click a column to sort.

How the topics were made

  • Network. Every paper of the tables is a node, the corpus of 1 to 10 authors and the collaboration papers alike; a link joins two papers when one cites the other (— links). This is the direct-citation approach of Waltman & van Eck (2012), used by CWTS for the OpenAlex topics, but nothing here is mapped to OpenAlex, arXiv or any other classification.
  • Topics. Leiden clustering (Traag, Waltman & van Eck 2019) maximizing modularity at resolution —, with igraph, up to 20 passes. Clusters under 100 papers join the cluster they share the most links with. Papers with no link (old records, theses, notes) get no topic.
  • Seeds. Leiden is randomized. Four runs with different seeds agree at NMI 0.84–0.85 and ARI 0.64–0.69 for topics; the run that agrees best with the others is kept. Small topics shift a little between runs, so their exact borders should not be over-read.
  • Areas. Leiden on the graph of topics, with the links inside each topic kept, at resolution —, the best of 50 runs; the four seeds agree at ARI 0.85–0.90.
  • Names. Each topic was named from the titles of its most cited papers (from INSPIRE), checked against its arXiv categories and journals.
  • Map. Topics are placed by a force layout of the graph of topics, each topic linked to its 6 strongest neighbours by association strength (links between two topics over the product of their total links).

Code: reproduce/topics/ of restrepo/inspireauth10, and the step log in .claude/skills/inspire-topics/SKILL.md.

Sources

Computed by reproduce/topics/ of restrepo/inspireauth10 from the tables in data/ (INSPIRE-HEP, CC0) and their citation network, clustered with Leiden (igraph 1.0, leidenalg 0.12). Built 2026-11-14. Self-contained page; d3 v7.9.0 (ISC licence) is included.

  • Totals (9 rows): Papers of the tables, papers with a topic and without one, topics, areas, citation links and the clustering resolutions. Download JSON
  • Areas (6 rows): The six areas: papers, topics, citations, arXiv mix, and papers in 2011-2015 and 2021-2025. Download JSON
  • Topics (304 rows): Each topic: name, area, papers (and those with 1 to 10 authors), citations, years, arXiv categories, journals and countries (shares), most cited papers, its position on the map, and its trend (Growing, Stable or Shrinking, by the change of its share of all papers from 2011-2015 to 2021-2025). Download JSON
  • Links between topics (1114 rows): Citation links between topics (each topic's 6 strongest by association strength), which place the topics on the map. Download JSON
  • Papers per year by topic (19152 rows): Papers of each topic by publication year. Download JSON
  • Papers per year by area (668 rows): Papers of each area by publication year. Download JSON
  • Author flows (13764 rows): For each topic, where its authors (INSPIRE profiles with 2 or more papers in the early period) had their main topic in the late period: the 15 largest destinations, the rest summed (to = -2), and those who stopped (to = -1), for three pairs of periods. Download JSON
  • Periods of the author flows (3 rows): The three pairs of periods of the author flows. Download JSON
  • Landmark papers (300 rows): The 300 most cited papers of the network (citations between papers of the tables), with the number of citing papers in each area, title, first author and arXiv number. Download JSON
  • Disruption of highly cited papers (7238 rows): Papers up to 2020 with 500 or more citations and 5 or more references in the network: CD index over the first 5 years (cd5, with n_i, n_j, n_k) and over all years (cd), with title, first author and arXiv number. Download JSON
  • Share of disruptive papers (102 rows): For each five-year bin and area (-1 = all), the papers with 100 or more citations and those with CD index above 0, over 5 years (cd5_pos) and all years (cd_pos). Download JSON
  • Areas by country (433 rows): Papers in each area of each country with 1,000 or more papers with a topic. Download JSON
  • Topics by country (17434 rows): Papers in each topic of each country with 1,000 or more papers with a topic. Download JSON
